parts.partSubtitle: Understanding energy flow and forces in natural and engineered systems.

units.title: Energy Flow from Earth's Systems
units.coreIdea: Investigates electrical energy transfer, system stability, and societal trade-offs through real-world energy infrastructure challenges.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: The Texas Power Crisis of February 2021.

units.title: Energy, Forces, & Earth's Crust
units.coreIdea: Explores how forces in Earth's interior drive surface changes through plate tectonics and energy transfer processes.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: The Sudden Rip in Earth's Crust in the Afar Triangle, Ethiopia (2005).

parts.partSubtitle: Analyzing motion, forces, and momentum in terrestrial and celestial contexts.

units.title: Vehicle Safety and Collisions
units.coreIdea: Applies momentum conservation and force analysis to understand and improve vehicle safety through engineering design.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: Puzzling Patterns in Traffic Collision Data (Decreasing Fatalities but Increasing Collisions).

units.title: Meteors, Orbits, and Gravity
units.coreIdea: Examines gravitational forces, orbital motion, and space object collisions to understand Earth's past and future risks.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: The Chelyabinsk Meteor Fireball over Siberia (2013).

parts.partSubtitle: Exploring wave properties, electromagnetic radiation, and their technological applications.

units.title: Radiation in Daily Life
units.coreIdea: Investigates electromagnetic radiation properties, wave-matter interactions, and safety considerations in modern technology.
units.anchoringPhenomenon: Microwave Ovens as Faraday Cages and Food Heating Without Obvious Heat Sources.

scheduling_notes.rotation_cycle: 4-day rotation where each class is dropped 2 out of 8 periods
scheduling_notes.class_frequency: Each class meets 3 out of every 4 instructional days
scheduling_notes.hive_days: Tuesdays and Thursdays have 20-minute HIVE periods with slightly shorter class periods (56-57 min vs 60 min)

units_covered.unit_name: Unit P.1: Energy Flow from Earth's Systems

anchoring_phenomenon.title: The Texas Power Crisis of February 2021
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Analyze the electrical energy transfer failures during the Texas blackouts to understand system stability, energy infrastructure design, and societal trade-offs in energy production and distribution.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Texas electricity demand and supply data, power outage satellite imagery, and energy source production data during the crisis.

units_covered.unit_name: Unit P.2: Energy, Forces, & Earth's Crust

anchoring_phenomenon.title: The Afar Triangle Rift Event (2005)
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Use seismic data and geological evidence to explain how forces in Earth's interior caused a sudden 60km crack in the crust, connecting nuclear processes to plate tectonics through energy transfer mechanisms.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Seismic wave arrival time data, tomography images of Earth's interior, and radioactive decay half-life data.

units_covered.unit_name: Unit P.3: Vehicle Safety and Collisions

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Traffic Collision Data Paradox
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Analyze why traffic fatalities are decreasing while collisions and injuries increase, investigating factors like distracted driving, vehicle design features, and safety technologies to propose community solutions.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Multi-year traffic collision statistics, reaction time experimental data, and crash test results for various safety features.

units_covered.unit_name: Unit P.4: Meteors, Orbits, and Gravity

anchoring_phenomenon.title: The Chelyabinsk Meteor (2013)
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Use orbital mechanics and gravitational principles to understand how the meteor's trajectory led to the explosive airburst over Siberia, and evaluate strategies for deflecting future potentially hazardous objects.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Near-Earth object tracking data, crater frequency data from Moon and Earth, and Chicxulub impact evidence.

units_covered.unit_name: Unit P.5: Radiation in Daily Life

anchoring_phenomenon.title: Microwave Ovens as Faraday Cages
anchoring_phenomenon.problem_description: Investigate why microwave ovens block cell phone signals while heating food without an obvious heat source, exploring electromagnetic radiation properties, wave-matter interactions, and safety considerations of modern wireless technology.
anchoring_phenomenon.provided_data: Electromagnetic spectrum data, microwave oven power measurements, and radiation exposure guidelines for various technologies.
